definitions: A strategy in which an investor borrows in a currency with a low interest rate and invests in a currency with a higher interest rate, profiting from the interest rate differential.
The practice of borrowing money at a low interest rate to invest in an asset that is expected to provide a higher return.
examples: The carry trade was popular before the financial crisis.
Many hedge funds engage in carry trade strategies.
A sudden shift in interest rates can unwind a carry trade quickly.
